newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Chernomyrdin says NATO-Russia deal possible May 27.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin says NATO-Russia deal possible May 27.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Monday an accord between Russia and NATO could be signed on May 27, but that Mocsow would remain opposed to the eastwards expansion of the alliance.

Asked at a news conference if the deal could be signed on May 27, as stated by President Boris Jeltsin last week, Chernomyrdin said laughing: "If the President said the 27th that means it will be ready on the 27th. As for NATO expansion, we will be against it even after that."
Yeltsin visited Germany last week and said he hoped the NATO-Russia pact would be ready for signing in Paris on May 27.
The Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland are the leading contenders to join the alliance in the first wave of new members.
Russia opposes NATO enlargement and wants a biding commitment that the alliance will not station new troops or weapons, including nuclear arms, in new member states.
"It is not a question of NATO. We are talking about the military components of NATO," Chernomyrdin said after talks with Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus.
Klaus said he understood Moscow's security concerns, but added that Czech NATO membership is "an expression of our interest in our security".
